rationale: part_of on the EXISTING preproc_include node type (R3 — no grammar change): an Objective-C `#import`/`#include` is FILE INCLUSION. The header's text is spliced into THIS translation unit, its declarations enter this file's scope, and it has no compilation unit of its own — the vocabulary's part_of contract (src/ast/types.ts:PartOf, 'a library unit INCLUDES a part file, one compilation unit'). `imports` already says the file depends on a header; it cannot say the header's text became part of this unit, so this label is ADDITIVE and the imports/references rows stay (the imports row is re-pinned below). THE TARGET IS SYMBOL-SHAPED, NEVER THE WRITTEN PATH: a path target is resolved by name against the symbol table and resolves zero rows (measured at 0 of 4,612 on the fleet's cpp include rows), so the target is the name a reader can look up — the framework/module for `<Framework/Header.h>` (first path segment) and the declared type's stem for a quoted `"LocalType.h"` — while the written path is preserved in metadata.partPath where it is metadata rather than identity. partRole is MANDATORY on every part_of row: 'library', because this file carries the directive and names the part. The negative half is the point: a clang `@import Module;` is a SEPARATELY COMPILED module imported by name, the opposite of spliced text, so it must produce no part_of row; and no part_of target may be a path.

expectRelationships.comment: framework header: the target is the MODULE (an identifier a consumer can resolve), the written path lives in partPath, and the row is import_based at 1.0 because the directive IS the syntax
quoted project header: the target is the declared type's stem — the name the rest of the file spells — not the path
`#include` is the same construct as `#import` here: both are preproc_include and both splice text
the part_of row is ADDITIVE: the imports dependency row keeps its written-path target and its own label, nothing is relabelled away

forbidRelationships.comment: PATH AS TARGET resolves zero rows — the exact failure this shape exists to avoid; the written path belongs in metadata.partPath
same for a quoted include: a header path is metadata, never identity
a clang module is a separately compiled unit imported by name, the OPPOSITE of textual inclusion — part_of would assert the header's text entered this unit
an #import is preprocessor scope, never a member of a class: file scope is the only source
same: a part_of row may not be sourced from a method body
